paper_metadata.title: Enhanced mechanical properties and thermal stability of hot-rolled Mo-0.5%ZrC alloy

evidence.quote: Enhanced mechanical properties and thermal stability of hot-rolled Mo-0.5%ZrC alloy
The Mo-0.5 wt% ZrC plates were prepared by powder metallurgical method.
The Mo-0.5 wt% ZrC plates were prepared by powder metallurgical method. Commercial Mo powder (average particle size ~2 μ m) and nanosized ZrC powder (average particle size ~50 nm)

Mo-0.5 wt%ZrC alloy plate with enhanced mechanical properties and thermal stability was manufactured by powder metallurgy and hot rolling. The as-rolled Mo-0.5%ZrC plate shows an ultimate tensile strength (UTS) of 725 MPa and a total elongation (TE) of 24.1% at room temperature.

Commercial Mo powder (average particle size ~2 μ m) and nanosized ZrC powder (average particle size ~50 nm) were ball-milled in a planetary ball mill at 260 rpm for 4 h under an argon atmosphere. WC balls and jars were used and the ball-to-powder ratio is 8:1.
The ball- milled powders were subsequently compacted by cold isostatic pressing at a pressure of 180 MPa
and then sintered in flowing dry hydrogen at 1900 ◦C for 4 h.

When the Ta is below 1300 ◦C, the Mo-0.5%ZrC samples mainly undergo the recovery stage. The annihilation of dislocations and the growth of subgrains cause a slow decrease in hardness from 246 HV to 230 HV.
When Ta is in the range of 1300 – 1500 ◦C, partial recrystallization occurs and the hardness decreases significantly to 175 HV after 1500 ◦C annealing.
Additionally, Mo-0.5%ZrC alloy exhibits a high recrystallization start temperature of about 1300 ◦C.
